# walletcap

> Spend limits for AI agent wallets that pay in USDC: a per-payment cap and a rolling 24-hour budget that holds across restarts, replicas on one host and payment rails. Published as `walletcap` on npm (Node 22.13+, TypeScript types included) and PyPI (Python 3.11+), Apache-2.0, with no runtime dependencies. Integrations for x402 clients, Coinbase CDP x402 spend controls, Coinbase AgentKit, the Coinbase Agentic Wallet CLI and payments MCP server, and Coinbase Spend Permissions.

- The wallet's owner creates the budget once: `npx walletcap set --wallet <address> --per-payment 50 --per-day 150`. Agents open it with `await openBudget({ wallet })` in JavaScript or `open_budget(wallet)` in Python. Opening never creates a budget unless `create: true` is passed, which is for demos and first-run setup.
- `await budget.pay(amount, fn)` in JavaScript, or `with budget.pay(amount):` in Python, holds the amount, runs the payment and settles it. A payment that throws stays held, noted unknown, unless it is marked as never sent: until one window past its settle-by time, or until its owner voids it. `budget.hold()` returns a `Hold` with `settle`, `void`, `settlesBy`, `settlesWithin` and `note`.
- The owner's handle is `openOwner()` / `open_owner()`, and the `walletcap` command: `set`, `freeze`, `unfreeze`, `status`, `history`, `holds`, `void <id>`, `void --all-unknown --older-than 24h` and `settle <id> --tx <hash>`. `walletcap check <dollars>` answers whether a payment would be paid right now (exit 0 or 1) and `walletcap doctor` checks the budget file's permissions, filesystem, format and triggers; both only read. In the library this is an API split, not an OS boundary.
- Errors, the same in both languages, with no common base: `BudgetUnavailable`, `BudgetRefused` (`code`, `brief`, `source`), `PaymentNotRecorded` and `UsageError`.
- The rule is SQL in `spec/schema.sql`, which both packages ship and run: payments are held, settled or void, rows are appended and never deleted, admission is one conditional insert, and the ledger reads its own clock. The count lives in one SQLite file per host. It is one host only: SQLite's locks aren't reliable over NFS, SMB or Docker Desktop bind mounts, and multiple hosts need a shared service, which isn't shipped yet.
- JavaScript integrations are subpath exports: `guard(client, budget)` from `walletcap/x402` for any `@x402/core` v2 client, including under `@x402/fetch`; `cdpStore(budget, { asset })` from `walletcap/cdp` as the `store` for Coinbase CDP's `applySpendControls`; `guardAgentKit(new X402ActionProvider(), budget)` from `walletcap/agentkit`; `guardAgenticWallet(budget, { request })` from `walletcap/agentic`, and `npx walletcap awal` for Coinbase's Agentic Wallet CLI. The payments MCP server runs behind `npx walletcap-mcp --wallet <address>`. Put one of `guard()` or `cdpStore()` on a client: with both, each payment counts twice.
- On chain: `AccountCapSpender` (Solidity, in `contracts/`) holds every Coinbase Spend Permission an account grants it to one rolling cap. It is unaudited; testnet only.
- Crash test: `npx walletcap-crash-test` runs offline and sends nothing. In eight runs on 6 November 2026, CDP's x402 controls set as Coinbase's README shows let $1,600–$1,700 and 1,000 EURC past a $150 cap across a restart, 10 replicas, a shared store and a payee who asks for EURC, and Spend Permissions let $300 past. walletcap's guard, its cdpStore and AccountCapSpender let $0.

## Docs

- [x402 spending limit for AI agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap/main/docs/x402-spending-limit.md): `guard()` on any x402 client, with `@x402/fetch`
- [Coinbase CDP x402 spend controls across replicas and restarts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap/main/docs/coinbase-cdp-spend-controls.md): `cdpStore()` as CDP's `SpendStore`
- [Coinbase AgentKit spending limit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap/main/docs/coinbase-agentkit-spending-limit.md): `guardAgentKit()` on AgentKit's `X402ActionProvider`
- [Coinbase Agentic Wallet and payments MCP budget](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap/main/docs/coinbase-agentic-wallet-budget.md): `npx walletcap awal` and `npx walletcap-mcp`
- [One cap across Coinbase Spend Permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap/main/docs/coinbase-spend-permissions-cap.md): the `AccountCapSpender` contract
- [Python spending limit for AI agent payments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap/main/docs/python-agent-spending-limit.md): the PyPI package

## README sections

- [Install and use](https://github.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap#install-and-use): install, the owner's one-time setup, JavaScript and Python usage, and one line per integration
- [How it counts](https://github.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap#how-it-counts): the states, the rule in SQL, and the ledger's clock
- [x402](https://github.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap#x402): the guard's rules for checking, holding and settling
- [Coinbase CDP spend controls](https://github.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap#coinbase-cdp-spend-controls): the store, and when to use it instead of the guard
- [Coinbase Agentic Wallet](https://github.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap#coinbase-agentic-wallet-awal-cli-and-mcp-server): the CLI wrapper and walletcap-mcp
- [Coinbase AgentKit](https://github.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap#coinbase-agentkit): `guardAgentKit()`
- [Coinbase Spend Permissions, on chain](https://github.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap#coinbase-spend-permissions-on-chain): `AccountCapSpender`
- [The owner's controls](https://github.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap#the-owners-controls): the owner's handle and the `walletcap` command
- [What it doesn't do](https://github.com/coriolislabs/WalletCap#what-it-doesnt-do): the enforcement tiers, one file per host, and payments it can't confirm
